entities.summary:
Gómez Suárez de Figueroa y Córdoba, 3rd Duke of Feria and 3rd Marquess of Villalba, was a pivotal Spanish grandee, diplomat, and military commander who served the Spanish Habsburg monarchy with distinction during the tumultuous early decades of the 17th century. Born into one of Spain's most ancient and powerful noble houses on December 30, 1587, in Guadalajara, his career unfolded against the backdrop of the Thirty Years' War, a conflict that fundamentally reshaped the geopolitical landscape of Europe. His actions in the Rhineland and Northern Italy were crucial in attempting to preserve the integrity of the Spanish Road, a vital military supply line connecting Habsburg territories from Italy to the Low Countries.

His career began with diplomatic service, including an embassy to France in 1618 and a significant mission to England in 1621 to negotiate the proposed marriage between Prince Charles and the Infanta Maria Anna, a complex endeavor that ultimately failed. Appointed Governor of Milan in 1625, Feria was thrust into the War of the Mantuan Succession (1628–1631), where he commanded Spanish forces, securing key positions and challenging French influence in Northern Italy. His military prowess was further demonstrated in 1633 when he led an army of 10,000 men from Italy across the Alps and through the Black Forest, a remarkable logistical feat, to relieve the besieged Habsburg stronghold of Breisach on the Rhine. This campaign temporarily stabilized the Habsburg position in Southwest Germany and opened a new front against Swedish and French forces.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Gómez Suárez de Figueroa's leadership as Governor of Milan and his daring military campaigns, especially the relief of Breisach in 1633, were crucial in temporarily securing the Spanish Road and preserving Habsburg influence in Central Europe during a critical phase of the Thirty Years' War.
